title: Becoming a GenAI solution architect: the three knowing
oneliner: Know the GenAI models on the market, know how to integrate them into existing projects, and know how to pick the right use case and the right model for it.
says: To pursue a career as a generative AI solution architect: know what generative AI models are available in the market; know how those models can be integrated cleanly with your existing projects; and know how to identify the right use case for your organization and the right model for that use case. He links a YouTube playlist for where to start.
explained: The three points escalate in seniority. Knowing the model landscape is homework - anyone can do it. Knowing integration is craft - APIs, data flow, latency, failure handling inside a system that already exists. Knowing use-case selection is judgment - the skill of saying no to AI where it does not pay, which is what organizations actually pay architects for.

Notice the order of his third point: use case first, model second. Amateurs fall in love with a model and hunt for a problem (get attached to a tool and then search for a use for it); architects start from the business problem and select the smallest model that solves it. That ordering echoes the inference-economy reel and recurs throughout his platform episodes.
takeaway: Sequence your growth: landscape knowledge, integration craft, then use-case judgment - and always choose the model after the problem.
